predecessors.name: Yuan dynasty
predecessors.text: the offshore islands and coast of Taizhou prefecture, Zhejiang, where Fang (born at Huangyan) took to the sea in 1348

successors.name: Zhu Yuanzhang's Wu
successors.text: Qingyuan (Ningbo), Taizhou, Wenzhou and de facto Shaoxing: He permanently controlled Qingyuan, Taizhou, and Wenzhou in Zhejiang by 1356

ledger.x: 1348: Fang Guozhen kills his accuser and takes to the sea.
By 1356: Fang holds Qingyuan, Taizhou and Wenzhou.
October 1367: Zhu Yuanzhang's armies attack Fang's coast.
October 1367: Zhu Liangzi's army takes Taizhou.
November 1367: Zhu Liangzi's army takes Wenzhou.
Late 1367: Tang He's fleet drives Fang out of Ningbo.
December 1367: Fang's coastal regime ends; he is treated well at Nanjing and dies there in 1374.

wars.name: Fang Guozhen's piracy against Yuan grain shipping
wars.outcome: No territorial result: Fang seized grain bound for Dadu (still doing so about 1349, which led Toqto'a to repair the Grand Canal), and in 1356 submitted to the Yuan and received titles.

wars.name: Zhu Yuanzhang's coastal campaign against Fang Guozhen
wars.outcome: Zhu wins: Taizhou (October), Wenzhou (November), Ningbo (Tang He's fleet), and Fang's surrender in December 1367.

certainty.note: Coastal prefectures and islands, a fleet state; the pages name prefectures, not frontiers.
